"'''Hot in Herre'''" is a song by American rapper [[Nelly]], released as the lead single from his second album, ''[[Nellyville]]'' (2002). It was released on May 7, 2002, by [[Universal Records (defunct record label)|Universal Records]]. The song was written by Nelly, [[Chuck Brown]], and the production duo [[the Neptunes]], and incorporates elements of Brown's 1979 single "[[Bustin' Loose (song)|Bustin' Loose]]", [[Neil Young]]'s 1972 song "[[Harvest (Neil Young album)#Side two|There's a World]]", and [[Nancy Sinatra]]'s 1966 cover of [[the Rolling Stones]]' "[[As Tears Go By (song)|As Tears Go By]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefader.com/2017/06/08/nelly-story-behind-hot-in-herre|title=Nelly Reveals The Secret History Behind The Timeless Smash 'Hot In Herre'|last=Starling|first=Lakin|date=June 8, 2017|access-date=January 27, 2024|work=[[The Fader]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Lauer |first=Jake |title=Nelly Talks 'Hot in Herre' 15 Years After His Monster Hit Topped the Charts |url=https://www.maxim.com/entertainment/nelly-interview-hot-in-herre-2017-6/ |website=[[Maxim (magazine)|Maxim]] |access-date=April 7, 2025 |date=June 13, 2017}}</ref> It features additional vocals by [[Dani Stevenson]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schiewe |first=Jessie |date=September 20, 2016 |title=Earworm Weekly: Nelly's 'Hot in Herre' |url=https://www.sfweekly.com/music/earworm-weekly-nelly-s-hot-in-herre/article_77b27021-f2a4-5e85-af6d-6e6414f30ce1.html |access-date=June 17, 2026 |website=[[SF Weekly]]}}</ref>

"Hot in Herre" is widely considered one of Nelly's signature songs, alongside follow-up single "[[Dilemma (Nelly song)|Dilemma]]".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nelly's 5 most 'valuable' songs |url=https://ew.com/music/nelly-catalog-most-valuable-songs/ |access-date=June 23, 2024 |website=EW.com}}</ref> The two singles became back-to-back [[List of Billboard Hot 100 number ones of 2002#Chart history|number-one hits]] on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosenbaum |first=Jason |date=October 26, 2011 |title=Nelly Has The Number One Song In The Country.... Nine Years Ago Today |url=https://www.riverfronttimes.com/music/nelly-has-the-number-one-song-in-the-country-nine-years-ago-today-2663473 |access-date=June 23, 2024 |website=Riverfront Times}}</ref> The song also reached number one in Canada and entered the top 10 in 12 additional countries.

"Hot in Herre" is a song by American rapper Nelly, released as the lead single from his second album, Nellyville (2002). It was released on May 7, 2002, by Universal Records. The song was written by Nelly, Chuck Brown, and the production duo the Neptunes, and incorporates elements of Brown's 1979 single "Bustin' Loose", Neil Young's 1972 song "There's a World", and Nancy Sinatra's 1966 cover of the Rolling Stones' "As Tears Go By". It features additional vocals by Dani Stevenson.

"Hot in Herre" is widely considered one of Nelly's signature songs, alongside follow-up single "Dilemma". The two singles became back-to-back number-one hits on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2002. The song also reached number one in Canada and entered the top 10 in 12 additional countries.

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
"Hot in Herre" premiered on April 15, 2002, several weeks before its official release, through [[AOL]] Music's First Listen online streaming service.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 12, 2002 |title=Billboard Bits: Mammoth/Hollywood, Nelly, Britney/Justin |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/billboard-bits-mammothhollywood-nelly-britneyjustin-76121/ |website=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref> It received more than 760,000 streams, setting a record for the website.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Singles Minded|last1=Pietroluongo|first1=Silvio|last2=Patel|first2=Minal|last3=Jessen|first3=Wade|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|volume=114|issue=18|page=55|date=May 4, 2002}}</ref>

The song peaked at number one in Canada, reached number four in the United Kingdom, and charted within the top 10 in several other international markets. In the United States, it became Nelly's first number-one hit on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and the Neptunes' first number-one hit as producers. It entered the Hot 100 on May 4, 2002, reached number one on June 29, and remained there until it was replaced by Nelly's follow-up single "[[Dilemma (Nelly song)|Dilemma]]" on August 10.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 4, 2002 |title=Hot In Herre / Nelly |url=https://elpee.jp/single/Hot%20In%20Herre/Nelly/ |access-date=June 17, 2026 |website=Billboard Database}}</ref> "Hot in Herre" ultimately finished at number three on the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2002|2002 Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles chart]].
sections.text:
"Hot in Herre" premiered on April 15, 2002, several weeks before its official release, through AOL Music's First Listen online streaming service. It received more than 760,000 streams, setting a record for the website.

The song peaked at number one in Canada, reached number four in the United Kingdom, and charted within the top 10 in several other international markets. In the United States, it became Nelly's first number-one hit on the Billboard Hot 100 and the Neptunes' first number-one hit as producers. It entered the Hot 100 on May 4, 2002, reached number one on June 29, and remained there until it was replaced by Nelly's follow-up single "Dilemma" on August 10. "Hot in Herre" ultimately finished at number three on the 2002 Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles chart.

sections.heading: Awards and accolades
sections.wikitext: At the [[45th Annual Grammy Awards]] in 2003, the song won the inaugural [[Grammy Award for Best Male Rap Solo Performance]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.grammy.com/grammys/awards/winners-nominees/255|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322203628/https://www.grammy.com/grammys/awards/winners-nominees/255|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 22, 2019|title=Grammy Awards Winners & Nominees for Best Male Rap Solo Performance|publisher=[[Grammy Awards]]|access-date=January 14, 2022}}</ref> In 2008, the song was ranked number 36 on [[VH1]]'s "100 Greatest Songs of [[Hip-hop|Hip Hop]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stereogum.com/24391/vh1s_100_greatest_hiphop_songs-2/lists/|title=VH1's 100 Greatest Hip-Hop Songs|last=Singh|first=Amrit|website=[[Stereogum]]|date=September 28, 2008|access-date=January 14, 2022}}</ref> In 2014, [[San Francisco]] radio station [[KVVF#Hot 105.7 (2014–2019)|Hot 105.7]] played the song on a continuous loop to promote its change from [[Latin music]] to [[rhythmic contemporary]]. The stunt lasted 72 hours and attracted media attention.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2014 |title=Nelly's "Hot in Herre" plays for over 72 hours on San Francisco radio station |url=https://acclaimmag.com/music/nellys-hot-herre-plays-72-hours-san-francisco-radio-station/ |access-date=June 30, 2022 |website=Acclaim Magazine}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Writers |title=This Radio Station Only Plays Nelly's 'Hot In Herre' |url=https://scenestr.com.au/music/this-radio-station-only-plays-nelly-s-hot-in-herre |access-date=June 30, 2022 |website=scenestr - Pop Culture & Entertainment|date=March 17, 2014 }}</ref>
sections.text: At the 45th Annual Grammy Awards in 2003, the song won the inaugural Grammy Award for Best Male Rap Solo Performance In 2008, the song was ranked number 36 on VH1's "100 Greatest Songs of Hip Hop". In 2014, San Francisco radio station Hot 105.7 played the song on a continuous loop to promote its change from Latin music to rhythmic contemporary. The stunt lasted 72 hours and attracted media attention.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: Two music videos were produced for song. The original, known as the "St. Louis Arch Version" and serviced to [[MTV Global|MTV Europe]], depicts a [[nightclub]] inside the [[Gateway Arch]] in [[St. Louis]] and features cameo appearances by [[Cedric the Entertainer]], [[Carmelo Anthony]], [[T. J. Duckett]], and [[Julius Peppers]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EiXWbi6GaHo&list=RDEiXWbi6GaHo |title=Hot In Herre (St. Louis Arch Version) (Official Music Video) |date=January 27, 2023 |last=Nelly |access-date=June 17, 2026 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> A second version, released in North America, is similarly set in a nightclub and features Cedric the Entertainer as a [[Disc jockey|DJ]] who briefly interrupts the song to announce a “fire” on the dance floor, though the crowd continues singing along.
sections.text: Two music videos were produced for song. The original, known as the "St. Louis Arch Version" and serviced to MTV Europe, depicts a nightclub inside the Gateway Arch in St. Louis and features cameo appearances by Cedric the Entertainer, Carmelo Anthony, T. J. Duckett, and Julius Peppers. A second version, released in North America, is similarly set in a nightclub and features Cedric the Entertainer as a DJ who briefly interrupts the song to announce a “fire” on the dance floor, though the crowd continues singing along.
